# Issue #7: touching intervals are not merged

`merge_intervals([(1, 3), (3, 5)])` returns `[(1, 3), (3, 5)]` but the documented
behaviour is that closed intervals sharing an endpoint merge into `[(1, 5)]`.
Unsorted input must also be handled. Fix `ranges/merge.py`.

content: All tests pass and edge cases behave correctly: touching intervals merge, unsorted input is handled, nested intervals collapse, and empty/single inputs work.

arguments.summary: Fixed merge_intervals in ranges/merge.py: (1) changed the merge condition from `start < last_end` to `start <= last_end` so closed intervals sharing an endpoint (e.g. (1,3) and (3,5)) merge into (1,5), and (2) rewrote the loop to iterate over the fully sorted input instead of assuming the first element is the smallest, so unsorted input is handled correctly. Both existing tests pass and manual checks confirm correct behavior for unsorted, nested, touching, empty, and single-interval inputs.
